title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues §1 of a set of foundational notes on divided powers, written for crystalline cohomology. A 'pseudo-anneau' is a commutative ring without unit. A pseudo-ring with divided powers carries maps π^n satisfying axioms 1.1–1.5.

This page defines a divided-power A-algebra: a pseudo-ring with divided powers that is also an A-algebra and satisfies 1.6, π^n(λx) = λ^n π^n(x) for λ in A. The marginal note says 1.6 holds automatically when A = Z. That is correct: from 1.2 one gets π^n(kx) = Σ π^{p_1}(x)…π^{p_k}(x) over compositions p_1+…+p_k = n with p_i ≥ 0. By 1.5bis each term equals the multinomial coefficient times π^n(x), and the multinomials sum to k^n.

Grothendieck then observes the following. If J is an ideal of a ring A, then J is a non-unital A-algebra. A PD structure on the ideal J is the same thing as a PD structure on this underlying A-algebra, i.e. a 'homogeneous' PD pseudo-ring structure satisfying 1.6.

§2. Let M be an A-module and Γ(M) = ⊕_{n≥0} Γ^n(M) its divided power algebra. The degree-1 maps π^n_{(1)} : x ↦ x^{(n)}, from M to Γ^n M, are to be extended to maps π^n : Γ^+(M) → Γ^+(M) sending Γ^p into Γ^{np}. The extension is forced by axiom 1.4: (x^{(p)})^{(n)} = (pn)!/((p!)^n n!) · x^{(pn)}. One then uses the universal property of Γ (polynomial laws) to define π^n on all of Γ^p(M).

The next page states that axioms 1.1–1.6 hold, so Γ^+(M) is the free PD algebra on M. It then constructs the PD envelope of a pair (A, I) as Γ_A(I) modulo relations. This is the standard foundational material of Roby and Berthelot.
errors: The text reads as if x ↦ π^n_{(p)}(x^{(p)}) were a homogeneous polynomial map of degree p from M to Γ^{np}(M). As a function of x it is homogeneous of degree pn. What the construction actually needs is π^n_{(p)} viewed as a homogeneous polynomial law of degree n on Γ^p(M), equivalently a linear map Γ^n(Γ^p M) → Γ^{np} M. This is a slip or compression.

Gap: Γ^p(M) is spanned by, but not equal to, the elements x^{(p)}. Extending π^n from these elements to all of Γ^p(M) requires checking compatibility with 1.2. Over general A with non-free M this is a genuine argument (Roby 1965, Berthelot). Here it is only asserted ('On vérifie').

ideas.what: Divided-power A-algebra (non-unital), with homogeneity axiom π^n(λx) = λ^n π^n(x), automatic for A = Z
ideas.modern_name: PD algebra / PD ideal (γ_n(λx) = λ^n γ_n(x))
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1966 letter/Crystals lectures (Dix exposés) use PD structures; foundations in Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407)

ideas.what: PD structure on an ideal J of A is the same as a PD structure on J viewed as a non-unital A-algebra
Extension of the divided powers from Γ^1(M) to Γ^+(M) via (x^{(p)})^{(n)} = (pn)!/((p!)^n n!) x^{(pn)}, making Γ^+(M) the free PD algebra on M
ideas.modern_name: Divided power algebra Γ_A(M) with its canonical PD structure (Roby's theorem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby, 'Les algèbres à puissances divisées', Bull. Sci. Math. 1965

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard foundational notes on divided powers (Cartan, Roby, Berthelot), written as preparation for crystalline cohomology. The page contains nothing beyond the published literature; the only point of interest is the 'pseudo-anneau' framing.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note reads 'N.B. C'est toujours vérifié si A = Z', referring to condition 1.6.
'x ∈ 𝔄' at the end of the formula line is likely 'x ∈ 𝔄' or 'x ∈ J', denoting the pseudo-ring; it is ambiguous in the image.
The line before 'satisfaisant 6.' reads roughly 'de pseudo-anneau homogène, à p.d. sur la ...', consistent with a homogeneous pseudo-ring with divided powers.
The struck text after Γ^{np}(M) (in the π^n_{(p)} line) is a crossed-out 'x ↦ x^{(n)}'.
The phrase 'application polynomiale homogène de degré p' is as written; mathematically it should be degree n on Γ^p(M), or degree pn on M.
